siemens-insights-hub-service-credentials.description: Insights Hub (formerly MindSphere) REST APIs via the regional gateway, authenticated with service credentials (OAuth2 client credentials issued in Settings → Service Credentials / Developer Cockpit).

siemens-insights-hub-technical-token-man.description: Insights Hub using application credentials and the Technical Token Manager (X-SPACE-AUTH-KEY). Use when your automation is registered as an application.

siemens-industrial-edge-management-iem.description: On-premises / cloud Industrial Edge Management portal API. Authenticates with a user login and uses the returned token. Self-signed certificates are common – enable "accept self-signed certificates" or add the CA.

generic-rest-api.description: Any HTTP API. Pick the auth type and add an OpenAPI specification for operation lookup.

postgresql-read-only.description: A PostgreSQL database (also Amazon RDS / Aurora PostgreSQL, Azure Database for PostgreSQL, Cloud SQL), read directly with SQL: access reviews of roles and grants, account hygiene, monitor checks (connection, replication lag, a query whose value is judged) and datasets. Every statement runs in a read-only transaction that is rolled back, with time, row and size limits; only one SELECT at a time is accepted. Set host, port, database and TLS under Platform → Database after creating it; credentials username and password of a read-only role (the GRANT statements are in docs/DATABASES.md). The outbound policy must allow host:port unless it is "platforms".

secretHelp.username: A read-only role (docs/DATABASES.md): pg_read_all_stats, SELECT on what processes read

mariadb-mysql-read-only.description: A MariaDB or MySQL database (also Amazon RDS / Aurora MySQL, Azure Database for MySQL), read directly with SQL: access reviews of users, roles and grants, account hygiene (locked and expired accounts, password age, default accounts), monitor checks (connection, replica lag, a query whose value is judged) and datasets. Every statement runs in START TRANSACTION READ ONLY and is rolled back, with time, row and size limits; only one SELECT at a time is accepted. Set host, port, database and TLS under Platform → Database after creating it; credentials username and password of a read-only account (docs/DATABASES.md).

secretHelp.username: A read-only account (docs/DATABASES.md): SELECT on the mysql tables Steward reads, REPLICATION CLIENT

microsoft-sql-server-read-only.description: A Microsoft SQL Server database (2016 or later, also Azure SQL Managed Instance and Amazon RDS for SQL Server), read directly with SQL: access reviews of logins, users, roles and permissions, account hygiene (sysadmins, disabled, locked and expired logins, password age, sa), monitor checks (connection, availability group lag, a query whose value is judged) and datasets. SQL Server has no read-only transaction: every statement runs in a transaction that is rolled back and the login must be read-only (db_datareader, VIEW SERVER STATE, VIEW ANY DEFINITION – docs/DATABASES.md). Only one SELECT at a time is accepted. Sign-in with a SQL login (user name and password); set host, port, database and TLS under Platform → Database.

secretHelp.username: A read-only login (docs/DATABASES.md): db_datareader, VIEW SERVER STATE, VIEW ANY DEFINITION

kafka-connect-connectors-read-only.description: A Kafka Connect cluster through its REST API, read-only (also with Debezium for change data capture): Steward reads the connectors with type, class, version, state and topics, their tasks with state, worker and the error of a failed task, and the installed plugins; monitors check that connectors and tasks run, a task that failed for N minutes, the lag of a sink connector and Debezium connectors whose topics got no message. Steward never creates, restarts, pauses or resumes a connector – changing requests are refused for this kind –, and every configuration it reads has its secret-looking values removed and is never stored. Base URL: the REST API (https://connect.example.com:8083); variable kafkaPlatform: the name or id of its Kafka platform (for topics and lag). Sign-in: basic (username/password), a bearer token, or a client certificate (tlsCertificate/tlsKey, mutual TLS). See docs/KAFKA.md.

secrets.tlsKey: Private key of the client certificate (PEM)

secretHelp.username: A user of the REST API that may read connectors (docs/KAFKA.md)

changedetection-io-page-watches-read-onl.description: A changedetection.io instance that runs separately – its own container, with its own browser for JavaScript pages – and watches pages without an API: vendor changelogs and release notes, terms and pricing pages, status pages, documentation. Steward reads its watches (title, URL, tags, last check, last change, errors, snapshot times) as components of the platform, links them to applications, services or vendors, and checks them in monitors (check "Page watch"); changedetection.io's notifications start processes through a webhook trigger. Read-only: Steward never writes and never reads page contents – only metadata and the link to the diff. Base URL: the instance's root (e.g. http://changedetection:5000 on the same Docker network); variable uiUrl: its address in the browser, for links, when it differs. API key: Settings → API in changedetection.io, sent as x-api-key. The outbound policy must allow the instance's host. Software versions are better watched by the version watch of the tech stack. See docs/CHANGEDETECTION.md.

secretHelp.apiKey: Settings → API in changedetection.io (with "Require API key" on)

data-contract-service-datacontract-cli-a.description: The datacontract CLI run as a web service ("datacontract api", MIT, https://cli.datacontract.com) – its own container next to Steward. Steward sends the ODCS contracts saved under Catalogue → Data contracts to POST /test, with the credentials of the tested server from its vault in the CLI's datacontract-* headers (per request, never in the contract), and stores the test run as evidence; POST /lint checks a contract with the CLI's own lint. Start the service with DATACONTRACT_CLI_API_KEY and enter the same key here (sent as x-api-key). The tested server is a database platform of Steward linked to the contract. Compose example and network rules: docs/DATA-CONTRACTS.md.

secretHelp.apiKey: The value of DATACONTRACT_CLI_API_KEY of the service (sent as x-api-key)

confluent-cloud-api.description: The Confluent Cloud API (https://api.confluent.cloud): Steward reads, read-only, the environments, Kafka clusters, Schema Registry clusters, service accounts, the metadata of API keys (owner, resource, created, expiry – never a secret) and the managed connectors with their tasks, every hour or on Read now; clusters link to the Kafka platform whose variable confluentClusterId names them; monitors check that clusters are provisioned and connectors and tasks run. With the variable schemaRegistryUrl and a key of that Schema Registry (registryKey/registrySecret) also its subjects. Access checks of source "Confluent" snapshot role bindings (and, with kafkaRestUrl, clusterId and the cluster's API key, its ACLs); platform costs read the Costs API. Credentials: a Cloud API key and secret of a service account – OrganizationAdmin reads everything. Steward's own reads only send GET; process steps may call the API – mark the identity read-only if Steward should never change anything. See docs/CONFLUENT.md.

secrets.registryKey: Schema Registry API key (optional, for subjects)
secrets.clusterApiKey: Kafka cluster API key (optional, for ACLs)
secrets.clusterApiSecret: Kafka cluster API secret (optional, for ACLs)

secretHelp.username: A Cloud API key (resource "Cloud resource management"), not a Kafka cluster key
secretHelp.registryKey: A key of the Schema Registry the variable schemaRegistryUrl names

title: Platforms
description: Connections to the APIs Steward calls – e.g. an Insights Hub tenant or a Kubernetes cluster – with base URL, credentials, API specifications and documentation. What runs where is described in the catalogue (applications and systems).

empty.title: No platforms yet
empty.text: A platform is one instance of a system you administer, for example your production Insights Hub tenant or an on-premises Industrial Edge Management. It stores the base URL, how to authenticate, encrypted credentials, API specifications (OpenAPI) and documentation. Processes then pick a platform for each connection when they run.

types.title: Connector types
types.hint: A connector type is a reusable template for a kind of system: authentication, variables, HTTP options, which credentials are needed, documentation links and API specifications – never credential values. Create one from a configured platform (platform page → menu → “Save as connector type”), export it as a file and import it on another installation. New platforms of that type get its API specifications automatically.
types.none: No custom connector types yet. Built-in presets: {{presets}}.
types.deleteHint: Delete connector type (existing platforms are not affected)
types.deleteConfirm: Delete connector type "{{name}}"? Existing platforms keep working.

addModal.title: Add platform – choose a starting point
addModal.hint: Everything can be changed later – presets only pre-fill authentication and URLs.

form.name: Name
form.credentialsHint: Leave fields empty that you don't need. You can add or replace credentials later.
form.authTypeHint: Chosen from the credentials you fill in (a token: bearer, user name and password: basic). Credentials of another type are stored but not sent.

detail.exportPostmanHint: Environment and a collection of the API operations (ZIP), without secrets
detail.tokenAge: Access token from {{fetched}}, expires {{expires}}. Roles granted since then need a new token.
detail.useOnly: You may use this platform in runs and send read-only requests. Changing its configuration, credentials or access requires the “manage” right.
detail.viewOnly: You may look at this platform but not use it in runs. Ask an administrator for access.
detail.deleteText: This deletes {{name}} including its stored credentials, API specs and documents. Processes and schedules that use it will fail until another platform is selected. The audit log is kept.

saveType.saved: Connector type "{{name}}" saved – it appears under Add platform and can be exported under Platforms → Connector types
saveType.hint: Stores authentication, variables, HTTP options, the names of the required credentials, documentation links and all API specifications of “{{name}}” as a reusable template. Credential values are never included.
saveType.kindHint: Short identifier, e.g. servicenow or my-mes. Processes can require this kind for a connection.
saveType.label: Label

credentials.info: Secrets are encrypted (AES-256-GCM) with a key derived from your master passphrase and never shown again or sent to the browser. Every change is recorded in the audit log (names only, never values). In processes they are available via <code/> and are masked in all logs.
credentials.readOnly: Only users who may manage this platform can change credentials.
credentials.replaces: This replaces the stored value of “{{key}}”.
credentials.removeText: Remove the secret {{key}}? Processes using it will fail until it is set again.

identities.none: This platform has no identity yet. Ask an administrator to review its connection settings.
identities.everyoneWithUse: Everyone with the “use” right on this platform

mcp.writes: Reads, and changing calls after approval ({{mode}})

identities.infoSeveral: An identity is one set of credentials of this platform, with its own access list, MCP mode, read-only flag and operation filter. Requests that name no identity use the default identity, which everyone with “use” on the platform may use. Every other identity is closed until you list who may use it. Steward’s checks add to – never replace – the rights the credentials have in the target system.
identities.addHint: Add an identity for credentials with other rights – for example a read-only one to make the default, and one for changes that only some people may use. The default identity’s credentials are also on the
identities.deleteText: Delete the identity “{{name}}” with its credentials? Schedules, triggers and monitors that name it keep it from being deleted.
identities.makeDefaultText: Make “{{name}}” the default identity? Everyone with “use” on the platform may use it then, and requests that name no identity use it. The current default identity becomes closed like any other identity.
identities.readOnlyHelp: Steward sends no changing request (POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE) with this identity – a POST that only reads only when the operation filter chooses it. Changing it back needs a confirmation.
identities.databaseReadOnly: Database platforms are read-only: every statement runs in a read-only transaction.
identities.authHelp: The same settings as the platform’s sign-in: type, token URL, scope … Its credentials are stored on the Credentials tab of this identity.
identities.authInvalid: Enter a JSON object with a sign-in type
identities.variablesHelp: These variables replace the platform’s for this identity (for example a user or role). Variables that decide where requests go cannot be set: {{fixed}}
identities.variableFixed: Decides where requests go – an identity cannot change it
identities.defaultAccess: The default identity is open to everyone with “use” on the platform. To narrow it, narrow the platform’s access – or make another identity the default.
identities.accessHelp: Who may use this identity: administrators, members of its owning teams who design or operate, and the entries below – each also needs “use” on the platform. Managing the platform does not make someone a user of this identity.
identities.mcpHelp: What MCP clients may do with this identity. Without an identity argument they use the default identity.
identities.noSpecs: An operation filter needs an API specification of this platform. Add one on the API specifications tab.
identities.filterHelp: Which operations requests through this identity may call. A request that matches no allowed operation is refused before it is sent – undocumented endpoints, other hosts and browser steps included.
identities.staleText: These chosen operations are no longer in the platform’s specifications and match nothing: {{list}}
identities.filterLimit: The filter sees the method and the path, not the body: a chosen POST /graphql also lets changes through. The rights of the credentials decide in the end.
identities.disabledText: This identity was added or changed outside Steward. It was kept when the platform's settings were confirmed, but it is disabled: nothing can use it and no credentials are sent with it. Read its settings and access list before an administrator enables it.
identities.enableText: Enable the identity “{{name}}”? Its credentials can be used again – by administrators, its owning teams and: {{who}}. Check its settings, credentials and access list first.
identities.privilegedHelp: Every use asks the person to confirm it is them (step-up): starting a run, saving a schedule or trigger, a request explorer call, approving an MCP request. Runs may wait for a second person. MCP clients never read with it, monitors never use it. Turning it off needs a confirmation.
identities.privilegedDefault: The default identity is never privileged: everyone with "use" on the platform uses it. Keep privileged credentials in another identity.
identities.registerMissingText: This privileged identity has no entry in the credentials register: document who owns it and when it is rotated.
identities.registerEmpty: No entry of the credentials register documents this identity.
identities.rotationHelp_one: Records today as the last rotation on the register entry that documents this identity.
identities.rotationHelp_other: Records today as the last rotation on the {{count}} register entries that document this identity.
identities.mcpPrivileged: This identity is privileged: MCP clients never read with it, and changing calls always need a second person (approved writes with four-eyes).

settings.kindHint: Processes can require a kind for a connection
settings.portalUrlHint: Start URL for browser automation (default: base URL)
settings.loginUrlHint: Absolute or relative to base URL
settings.insecureTlsHint: Common for on-premises Industrial Edge Management. Prefer adding the CA certificate below.
settings.proxyHint: Empty = HTTPS_PROXY / NO_PROXY environment, 'none' = direct, or a URL
settings.maxConcurrencyHint: Calls to this platform at the same time
settings.retryNonIdempotentHint: Only turn on if the API handles repeated requests safely – they may create or change data twice.
settings.unsentCredentials: Authentication is set to “None”, but credentials are stored ({{keys}}): they are not sent, and the platform will answer 401. Choose “{{type}}” if the API needs them.
settings.bearerHeaderHint: Default: Authorization: Bearer <token> (GitLab: PRIVATE-TOKEN: <token>). Another header name sends the token as it is; Authorization on GitLab is for OAuth tokens.
settings.destinationKeepTitle: Send the stored credentials to the new address?
settings.destinationKeepText: The changed settings send the credentials of “{{name}}” somewhere else. Keep them only if you trust the new address; otherwise remove them and enter them again for it.
settings.destinationClearTitle: The stored credentials will be removed
settings.destinationClearText: The changed settings send the credentials of “{{name}}” somewhere else, so they are removed when you save. Enter them again under Credentials afterwards.
settings.variablesHint: Non-secret values such as tenant or region. Usable in URLs as {{url}}, in processes as {{conn}} or {{pvar}}.
settings.missingSecrets: missing: {{keys}} (add them on the Credentials tab)
settings.clientAuthAssertion: Client assertion signed with a certificate (privateKey, certificate)
settings.tokenRequestHint: A login call is made first; the token is extracted from its response and added to every API call. Use {{secrets}} and {{vars}} in URL, headers and body.
settings.retriesHint: Requests that fail with 429, 502, 503, 504 or a network error are repeated with growing delays (honouring Retry-After). Empty fields use the defaults.
settings.trustedOriginsHint: Credentials are only sent to the base URL's origin. Add further origins (https://host[:port]) that belong to this platform and may receive them, e.g. a separate gateway host. Requests to other hosts are sent without credentials.
settings.jwtHint: Steward signs a JWT with the private key (credential privateKey; encrypted keys also privateKeyPassphrase), valid for at most an hour. Claims are templates ({{vars}}); {{fingerprint}} is the public key fingerprint Snowflake expects. iat, exp and jti are set by Steward.
settings.jwtModeToken: Send the JWT as the token
settings.jwtModeExchange: Exchange it for an access token (RFC 7523)
settings.awsHint: Every request to the platform is signed with the access key (credentials accessKeyId and secretAccessKey, optionally sessionToken). With a role, Steward assumes it and signs with its temporary credentials (renewed before they end).
settings.awsRoleArnHint: Read-only role; the access key only needs sts:AssumeRole

specs.importHint: OpenAPI 3.x or Swagger 2.0, JSON or YAML. Operations become searchable here and can be picked in the explorer.
specs.name: Name (optional)
specs.title: Specifications
specs.prefixHint: Put in front of every operation path, relative to the platform base URL. Taken from the specification's server URL on import. Leave it empty if the base URL already contains it.
specs.prefixInvalid: Use /segment/segment with letters, digits and . _ ~ - only (no .. segments, at most 200 characters), or leave it empty.
specs.clickHint: Click an operation to try it in the explorer.
specs.truncated: Showing the first {{count}} – refine the search.
specs.noOperations: The imported specifications contain no operations.
specs.copyHint: Each platform gets its own copy – later changes to one don't affect the others, since platforms of one kind can run different API versions. Only platforms of the kind {{kind}} that you may manage are offered.
specs.copyNoTargets: There is no other {{kind}} platform you may manage.
specs.copyReplace: Replace a specification with the same title and version (it keeps its id, so processes using it keep working)
specs.copySkippedSource: {{name}}: this is the platform it comes from – skipped
specs.addBuiltInHint: The API description Steward brings for this kind of platform – for assistants (MCP gateway) and process steps.
specs.builtInPresent: The built-in specification is already there

docs.title: Title
docs.notePlaceholder: e.g. Runbook: how to rotate service credentials…
docs.fileHint: PDF, Word, text… up to 50 MB
docs.none: No documentation yet. Keep runbooks, API manuals and useful links next to the platform.

explorer.title: Ad-hoc request
explorer.hint: Calls are authenticated with the platform's credentials and every call is recorded in the audit log. Path placeholders like {{example}} from a spec must be replaced by real values.
explorer.confirm: I understand this changes data on {{name}}

integrity.title: Connection settings changed outside Steward
integrity.text: The base URL, authentication or other connection settings of this platform no longer match their seal: they were changed directly in the database. To protect its credentials, no requests are sent to it. Current base URL: {{url}}
integrity.confirmQuestion: Confirm the current connection settings (base URL {{url}})? Check the settings and the audit log first.
integrity.askAdmin: Ask an administrator to review and confirm the settings.

review.reset: Its credential source (reserved for a later PAM checkout) is not used yet – it is removed when you confirm.
review.remove: This identity is removed when you confirm.
review.access: Who may use it besides administrators and its owning teams: {{subjects}}
review.disable: Added or changed outside Steward: it is kept, but disabled when you confirm – no credentials are sent with it until an administrator enables it after reading its access list.

recordings.title: Recorded responses
recordings.help: Answers of this platform for test runs: a test run of a process or monitor uses them instead of calling the platform and names every call without one. Real runs and dry runs never use them. They can hold personal data – everyone who may use the platform sees them.
recordings.emptyHint: Record one in the API explorer (Save as recorded response) or enter it here, e.g. copied from Swagger or Postman.
recordings.removeConfirm: Remove the recorded response for {{request}}? Test runs that use it fail at this call.
recordings.redactionHint: The platform's credentials are replaced by *** and headers with credentials or cookies are dropped when you save.
recordings.pathHint: As in process steps, relative to the base URL. {id} matches one segment, a trailing * the rest.
recordings.queryHint: One per line: name=value. The request must have them; others may be there too.
recordings.bodyMatchHint: Parts of the request body the request must have, e.g. {"user": "u2"}. Empty: any body.
recordings.bodyHint: JSON, or any text for an answer that is not JSON. At most {{mb}} MB.

wizard.title: Add a platform
wizard.searchPlaceholder: Name or kind, e.g. Snowflake or git
wizard.noMatch: No connector matches. Clear the search, or start from the generic REST API.
wizard.secretsKept: Credentials entered before are kept – fill in only the ones to change.

hints.title: What usually helps
hints.credentials: The platform did not accept the credentials: check the key, token or password (and that it has not expired), and the sign-in type.
hints.forbidden: Signed in, but not allowed: give the technical user or token the read rights the connector’s documentation lists.
hints.baseUrl: Nothing at this address: check the base URL – it is the API, often with a path such as /api/v4 – and the test path.
hints.apiUrl: The address answers with a web page, not the API: use the API’s base URL (see the connector’s description).
hints.signIn: The address leads to a sign-in page: the API must be reachable without browser sign-in – use the API endpoint or a technical user.
hints.dns: The host name could not be resolved: check the spelling, and the DNS or proxy settings of the server.
hints.reach: The server could not connect: check host and port, firewalls and the proxy under the platform’s HTTP settings.
hints.outbound: The outbound policy blocked the address: an administrator allows it under Settings → Outbound access.
hints.tls: The certificate was not accepted: add the private CA under the platform’s HTTP settings (or allow self-signed certificates for a test).
hints.timeout: No answer in time: the platform may be slow or the address may be unreachable from the server.

wizard.databaseHint: TLS certificate, limits and the connection pool can be set later under Database.

start.intro: What you can do with “{{name}}” in Steward – one click each.
start.nothing: No templates, monitors or access checks read this kind of platform directly. Processes can call its API in HTTP steps.
start.bundlesHint: Processes, a dashboard and their schedules that belong together.
start.allTemplates: Show them in the template gallery
start.monitorExamples: Examples: {{names}} (Monitors → Import → From the example library)
start.accessHint: Snapshot who has which access, compare it with the documented changes, and include it in person reviews.
start.mcpHint: Let AI assistants read this platform’s API through the MCP gateway – changes need a person’s approval.

health.failingSince: Failing since {{when}} – the platform’s managers were notified.
health.periodicHint: When the test starts failing, the platform’s managers get “Platform connection failing” (routed like other notifications).

ai.intro: The models processes may ask through this gateway (step “Ask an AI model”), each in the request format the gateway expects for it, and the data the gateway may be sent. Limits and budgets: tab “AI usage”.
ai.noModelsHint: Read the gateway’s model list or add a model by hand; processes can only ask models listed here.
ai.noModelsReadOnly: People who manage this platform add the models.
ai.removeModelText: Processes that ask {{model}} through this gateway fail until it is set up again. The usage stays in the log.
ai.notSaved: The AI settings were not saved
ai.idTaken: This model is set up already
ai.outputTooLarge: Must be smaller than the context window
ai.pathInvalid: A path that starts with /, without a query

fields.idHint: As the gateway expects it in the request (or in the path of the Converse format)
fields.label: Shown as (optional)
fields.formatHint: Which of the gateway’s endpoints this model is asked through
fields.pathHint: Another path than the format’s, relative to the base URL; {modelId} is replaced
fields.maxOutputHint: Default and ceiling of one call
fields.maxInputHint: Default: the context window minus the output
fields.charsPerTokenHint: For the estimate before a call; default 3.5
fields.modelsPathHint: Where the gateway lists its models (OpenAI list format)
fields.prices: Prices (optional, in your currency – for reports)

ai.discoverHint: What GET {{path}} lists. The format is a suggestion – the gateway’s documentation says which endpoint serves which model.
ai.discoverFailed: The gateway did not list its models

allowed.title: Allowed data
allowed.intro: What processes may send to this gateway. What is checked is the value sent, whichever step wrote it: a value read from a platform carries that platform’s data; a computed one (set variables, for each, sub-processes) counts as carrying everything of its run – the data of every platform, its inputs and the datasets it reads. Nothing is allowed until you allow it.
allowed.nothing: Nothing may be sent yet: steps that ask a model through this gateway fail with AI_DATA_NOT_ALLOWED.
allowed.platformsHint: The platforms whose answers may be sent
allowed.datasetsHint: Keys or patterns such as checkmk.*; * allows every dataset the run may read
allowed.inputsHint: Values people or triggers give when a run starts

aiUsage.intro: Every call of a model through this gateway counts against the budgets of the installation, of this gateway and of its process – per day and per month (UTC). At 80 % a notification goes out; a call whose estimated input plus its most output no longer fits is refused before it is sent (AI_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED). The log holds no prompts and no answers.
aiUsage.editHint: Tokens (input and output together) per calendar day and month in UTC. Leave a field empty for no limit.
aiUsage.commentHint: Kept in the audit log with the change
aiUsage.raiseHint: Raising a budget (or removing its limit) asks you to confirm it is you.
aiUsage.otherProcess: A process you may not see
aiUsage.processBudgetsHint: Count the process’s calls through every gateway.
aiUsage.noProcessBudgets: No process has a budget of its own.
aiUsage.noCallsHint: The connection test and every run of a step “Ask an AI model” show up here.

database.intro: The connection of this database platform. Every statement runs read-only, in a transaction that is rolled back, within the limits below. User name and password are credentials (Credentials tab).
database.notSet: No connection yet: enter the host and the database and save, then test the connection.
database.notSetReadOnly: No connection yet. People who manage the platform set it here.

databaseHint.mysql: The default database (schema); catalog queries read the server's accounts
databaseHint.sqlserver: The database whose users, roles and permissions are read

database.hostHint: Host name or IP address, without scheme or port
database.credentialsHint: Sign-in: the credentials username and password of a read-only account – the GRANT statements per database system are in docs/DATABASES.md.

tlsModeHints.verify: Encrypted; the certificate and the host name are checked
tlsModeHints.require: Encrypted, but any certificate is accepted

tlsWarning.require: Without verification, a server that pretends to be the database can read the password. Use it only for a test system, or add the CA certificate and verify.
tlsWarning.off: Without TLS, the password and every result travel in clear text. Use it only on a trusted local network.

database.caHint: For a private CA; the system's CAs are trusted as well
database.serverNameHint: When the certificate names another host than the one connected to
database.limitsHint: Ceilings for every statement on this platform – steps can lower them, not raise them. Empty: the default.

readOnly.postgresql: PostgreSQL: the session is read-only (default_transaction_read_only) and every statement runs in BEGIN TRANSACTION READ ONLY, then ROLLBACK.
readOnly.mysql: MariaDB / MySQL: the session is SET SESSION TRANSACTION READ ONLY and every statement runs in START TRANSACTION READ ONLY, then ROLLBACK.
readOnly.sqlserver: SQL Server has no read-only transaction: every statement runs in a transaction that is rolled back – the login itself must be read-only (db_datareader, VIEW SERVER STATE, VIEW ANY DEFINITION).

database.docsLink: Read-only roles and what Steward refuses (docs/DATABASES.md)
database.notSaved: The connection could not be saved
database.contractServiceUnverified: Allow the data contract service to connect without certificate verification
database.contractServiceUnverifiedHint: The data contract service cannot verify the certificate of PostgreSQL and MySQL. Without this, data contract tests of this platform are refused while TLS is on. Off by default; the change is audited.

schema.title: Database schema
schema.helpPlatform: Tables, views, columns, keys and indexes of this database. Every read or tbls import is a snapshot; Steward shows what changed between them and which changes are breaking.
schema.helpSystem: Tables, views, columns, keys and indexes of the database on this system, from tbls imports. Every import is a snapshot; Steward shows what changed between them and which changes are breaking.
schema.exportHint: Open the file in an editor such as dbdiagram, drawDB, ChartDB or Azimutt.
schema.readFirst: Read: the first snapshot is stored
schema.readFailed: The schema could not be read
schema.scheduled: Read every {{hours}} h · the newest {{keep}} snapshots are kept
schema.systemIsPlatform: This system is a database platform of Steward: its schema is on the platform.
schema.systemIsPlatformLink: This system is a database platform of Steward – its schema is on the platform:
schema.emptyPlatform: Read the database, or import the schema.json of tbls. Each read and import becomes a snapshot.
schema.emptySystem: Import the schema.json of tbls for this database – as a file here, or from CI through the API.
schema.whoPlatform: Who may use the platform reads it; its managers import a tbls schema.
schema.whoSystem: Who may change the system imports its schema.
schema.olderSnapshot: You are looking at the snapshot of {{when}}.
schema.truncated: The database has more tables or columns than Steward keeps: this snapshot holds the first ones.
schema.noTablesHint: Try another name, or search for a column.
schema.noChangesYetHint: The next read or import shows what changed against this snapshot.
schema.incomplete: A snapshot is truncated: removed tables, columns and keys cannot be told from the ones left out, and are not listed.
schema.sameSchema: The two snapshots hold the same schema.
schema.checksHint: Findings of tbls lint, named by their rule (configured in .tbls.yml).
schema.importHelp: The schema.json that tbls writes (tbls out -t json), and optionally the output of tbls lint. Steward checks the file against the tbls format and records its SHA-256 in the audit log.
schema.lintHint: The output of tbls lint becomes checks with their rule names.
schema.importFailed: The schema could not be imported
schema.importedUnchanged: Imported: the schema is unchanged, no new snapshot
schema.previewUnchanged: The same schema as the newest snapshot: the import adds none.
schema.previewChanges_one: Against the newest snapshot: {{count}} change, {{breaking}} breaking.
schema.previewChanges_other: Against the newest snapshot: {{count}} changes, {{breaking}} breaking.
schema.previewFirst: The first snapshot of this database.
schema.fromCiHelp: Run tbls where the database is and push its file with a push token of this database (Push from CI, below).
schema.retentionHint: The newest ones (1 to {{max}}); older ones are removed.
schema.intervalHint: 0: only when someone reads it, or a monitor check does.
schema.settingsNotSaved: The settings could not be saved
schema.pageHelp: The tbls imports of this system, what changed between them, and the exports.

push.title: Push from CI
push.help: A push token can do one thing: push the tbls schema.json of this database (and the output of tbls lint) from a CI job. It is shown once and stored as a hash, and stops working when the person who created it is deactivated or may no longer manage this database.
push.emptyHint: Create one for the CI job that runs tbls, and keep it as a secret there.
push.name: Name
push.nameHint: Where it is used, e.g. “GitHub Actions, main”
push.addressesHint: IP addresses or CIDR ranges the push may come from; empty: any.
push.creatorInactive: Creator inactive – create a new token
push.creatorInactiveHint: {{name}} created it and is deactivated or may no longer manage this database: pushes with it are refused.
push.rotateConfirm: Rotate the push token “{{name}}”? The current secret stops working at once.
push.revokeConfirm: Revoke the push token “{{name}}”? Pushes with it are refused from now on.
push.secretOnce: Copy the token now: Steward shows it only this once and keeps only its hash.
push.secretHelp: Keep it as a secret of the CI job (STEWARD_PUSH_TOKEN) and push with one of these commands.

connect.title: Connectors
connect.help: What Steward last read from the Kafka Connect REST API, read-only: connectors, their tasks and the installed plugins. Read every hour and with Read now. Steward never restarts, pauses or resumes a connector.
connect.readFailed: Kafka Connect could not be read
connect.kafkaPlatformMissing: The variable kafkaPlatform names no Kafka platform you may see – topics and lag cannot be linked.
connect.kafkaPlatformNone: No Kafka platform linked (variable kafkaPlatform) – topics are not linked to topic components.
connect.readError: The last read failed ({{when}}) – the connectors shown are from the read before
connect.emptyHint: Read now reads the connectors, tasks and plugins of the cluster.
connect.emptyReadHint: The cluster has no connector, or the account may not list them.
connect.who: Who may use the platform reads it.
connect.configHint: Read from Kafka Connect now and not stored. Values that look secret (passwords, tokens, keys, credentials, sasl.jaas.config …) are removed; reading is recorded in the audit log.
connect.noDatabase: No database platform or system matches (or you may not see it)
connect.traceHint: Shortened; values that look secret are removed.

confluent.readFailed: Confluent Cloud could not be read
confluent.read: Read {{when}} · every hour and with Read now
confluent.readError: The last read failed – the values before it are shown
confluent.partErrors: Parts that could not be read (their last values are shown)
confluent.notReadHint: Read now reads the environments, clusters, connectors, service accounts and API keys of the organisation.
confluent.clustersHelp: The environments and Kafka clusters of the Confluent Cloud organisation, read-only through the Cloud API. A cluster belongs to the Kafka platform whose variable confluentClusterId names it – its topics, consumer lag and costs are there.
confluent.noClustersHint: The organisation has no cluster, or the Cloud API key may not list them (OrganizationAdmin, or EnvironmentAdmin on each environment).
confluent.noKafkaPlatform: None – set confluentClusterId on a Kafka platform
confluent.kafkaPlatformHint: To read a cluster's topics, lag and schemas, add a Kafka cluster platform with its bootstrap servers and set its variable confluentClusterId to the cluster id (lkc-…).
confluent.schemasHelp: The Schema Registry clusters of the environments and – with the variable schemaRegistryUrl and a key of that registry (registryKey, registrySecret) – its subjects with their versions and compatibility. Read-only.
confluent.noRegistryHint: Set the variable schemaRegistryUrl to a Schema Registry's endpoint (listed above) and its API key in registryKey and registrySecret under Credentials. The outbound policy must allow the endpoint.
confluent.subjectsTruncated: Not every subject was read in full: versions and compatibility are read for the first 200 subjects.
confluent.subject: Subject
confluent.connectorsHelp: The fully managed connectors of every cluster with their tasks and the error of a failed one, read-only – Steward never creates, pauses, resumes or deletes a connector and keeps no configuration. Their topics link to the Kafka topic components of the cluster's Kafka platform.
confluent.noConnectorsHint: The clusters have no managed connector, or the Cloud API key may not list them.
confluent.keysHelp: The organisation's API keys with owner, resource, creation and expiry – metadata only: Confluent never returns a secret in this list, and Steward keeps none. Listing API keys needs OrganizationAdmin.
confluent.keysHidden: Only who may use the platform sees its service accounts and API keys.
confluent.noKeysHint: The organisation has no API key, or the Cloud API key may not list them (OrganizationAdmin).
confluent.keysHint: Confluent's API does not say when a key was last used. A key older than a year has a rotation hint; one that expires within 30 days is marked.
confluent.registerKey: Add the API key {{key}} to the credentials register
confluent.keyEntryDescription: Confluent Cloud API key "{{name}}" of {{owner}} for {{resource}}

watches.intro: The watches of changedetection.io are the components of this platform: Steward reads their title, page, tags, last check, last change and errors – never the page contents. Link a watch to an application, a service or a vendor; the monitor check "Page watch" judges them.
watches.lastRead: Read {{when}} by {{who}} · {{count}} watches · read again every hour
watches.emptyText: changedetection.io has no watches yet. Add the pages to watch there; Steward shows them here at the next read.
watches.notReadText: Read the watches once; Steward then reads them again every hour with your rights.
watches.whoCanRead: People who may use this platform read its watches.
watches.limited: Showing {{shown}} of {{total}} watches: Steward keeps at most {{max}} per platform.
watches.linkIntro: The watch then shows up with the application or service (under "Linked from"), and the vendor names whose page it is.
watches.vendorHint: Whose page it is, e.g. the vendor of a cloud service
watches.historyNote: Only the times: the snapshots themselves stay in changedetection.io.

identitySelect.label: Identity
identitySelect.description: Which credentials of the platform are used – the default identity unless you choose another
identitySelect.privilegedHint: A privileged identity: you confirm it is you when you start – and a second person may have to approve the start.
